answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is never a free handle but an onyx cut from hard rock. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations across the dune. Every seat costs real compute, so cheap mass registration stalls — a pigment of fake identities can't be painted on for free.
